about.body: The N47 is BMW's 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder diesel engine, produced from 2007 to 2016. It's the direct successor to the M47 and was used extensively across the BMW range during its production run. The N47 appears in six model lines — the 1 Series, 3 Series, 4 Series, 5 Series, X4 and X5 — making it one of the more widely-deployed diesel engines of its era. The N47 is a common-rail diesel with a cast-iron block and aluminium cylinder head, featuring BMW's variable geometry turbocharger and the brand's third-generation common-rail injection system. It was offered in multiple power outputs across different applications, from the 116d's entry-level tune up to the higher-output versions used in the 320d and 420d.

byModel.body: Across the 1 Series (E87/E88, 2007–2012), the N47 powered the 116d, 118d and 120d variants. The 3 Series (E90/E91/E92/E93, 2007–2012) used it in the 318d and 320d — one of the most common N47 applications we see. The 4 Series (F32/F33/F36, 2013–2016) carried it in the 418d and 420d, representing the later production years for this engine. The 5 Series (F10/F11, 2010–2016) used the N47 in the 518d and 520d. The X4 (F26, 2014–2016) used it in the xDrive20d, and the X5 (E70, 2008–2013) used it in the xDrive30d.

compatibility.body: Because the N47 spans six different models and multiple generations across a nine-year production run, compatibility comes down to confirming your exact model, generation, and drivetrain spec, which we do by registration. An N47 from a 3 Series isn't a drop-in match for an N47 from an X5 — ancillaries, mounting, and drivetrain configuration all differ. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm your exact vehicle. BMW N47 Symptoms That Justify Inspection The following symptoms don't automatically mean the N47 requires a rebuild. Proper diagnosis comes first. Knocking or rattling noises Low oil pressure warning Excessive smoke Coolant loss Overheating Misfire or rough running Loss of compression Metal contamination in oil Engine seizure Warning lights Loss of power
